section_summary: This section concerns applications and military clearances for travel to occupied Japan by diplomats, missionaries, businesspeople, and family members. It documents SCAP entry procedures, national business quotas, passport and alien-departure requirements, and several approvals, refusals, or pending cases. It also includes correspondence concerning Argentine repatriates in Okinawa and applications routed through Irish, Lebanese, Swiss, Syrian, Indian, Iranian, Czech, and other representatives.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning Denise Anne Bickart's return to Japan
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains that Bickart needs French-sponsored SCAP entry clearance rather than a United States exit permit.
subfiles.summary: Bickart is directed to obtain Japanese entry authorization through the French representative in Japan and consult the French Embassy.

subfiles.title: Request for entry permission for Enrique Bravo
subfiles.about: Forwards Mexico's application for Enrique Bravo to serve as its commercial representative in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The State Department asks military authorities to obtain an early SCAP decision on Bravo's proposed commercial assignment.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Father O'Brien's Japan permission
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records confirmation to the Irish Legation that Father O'Brien had been cleared for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg treated her telephone explanation of O'Brien's clearance and documentation as acknowledgment of the Irish note.

subfiles.title: Irish Legation note concerning Joseph Francis O'Brien
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Ireland
subfiles.about: Requests confirmation that SCAP granted Father O'Brien permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Irish Legation cites information from Bruno Bitter and asks for prompt confirmation of O'Brien's clearance.

subfiles.title: Military decision on Victor and Fadhila Moche
subfiles.about: Reports that travel by Victor and Fadhila Moche to Japan is not favorably considered.
subfiles.summary: The Civil Affairs Division declines to support the Moches' travel at this time.

subfiles.title: Instruction reporting refusal of the Moches' travel
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Baghdad
subfiles.about: Directs the Baghdad mission to notify Victor Moche that his and his wife's travel was not approved.
subfiles.summary: The mission is instructed to communicate the military authorities' unfavorable decision to Victor Moche.

subfiles.title: Lebanese request for Japanese-entry application forms
subfiles.about: Requests additional Form DS-513 applications for Lebanese commercial travelers to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Lebanese Legation asks the Department for several Japanese-entry application forms.

subfiles.title: Reply enclosing forms for the Lebanese Legation
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Lebanese request and encloses six sets of Japanese-entry forms.
subfiles.summary: Six sets of Form DS-513 are supplied to the Lebanese Legation.

subfiles.title: Return of Denise Bickart's application
subfiles.about: Returns Bickart's application because the office no longer handles French nationals under Circular No. 8.
subfiles.summary: French applicants must pursue entry permission through their national authorities rather than the United States military-permit office.

subfiles.title: Military-permit application for Denise Anne Bickart
subfiles.from: E. B. Hutchison, Exit Permit Unit
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Bickart to travel to Kobe and rejoin her husband.
subfiles.summary: The form records Bickart's French nationality, passport, destination, and family-reunification purpose.

subfiles.title: Affidavit of Denise Anne Bickart
subfiles.about: Describes Bickart's Japanese residence, wartime internment, health trip, and wish to rejoin René Bickart.
subfiles.summary: Bickart swears that she seeks to resume residence with her husband at Shioya near Kobe.

subfiles.title: Alien departure application of Denise Anne Bickart
subfiles.about: Applies to depart the United States for permanent residence with her husband near Kobe.
subfiles.summary: The application supplies Bickart's biography, passport, residence, finances, references, destination, and sworn declaration.

subfiles.title: Processing note on the Franklin reply
subfiles.about: Notes delayed typing and questions revising the Franklin reply because of an October 1 sailing.
subfiles.summary: The writer flags timing problems affecting the response to Mrs. Franklin.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting expedited permits for the Franklin family
subfiles.about: Requests help obtaining passports and military permits so she and her son can join her husband in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Franklin describes slow mission-board paperwork and asks Anderson to expedite clearance before the planned October sailing.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mrs. Franklin concerning issued documents
subfiles.about: Reports that Franklin's passport and military permit were issued September 18.
subfiles.summary: Caldwell wishes Franklin a successful voyage and conveys Anderson's greetings to Henry Jones.

subfiles.title: Letter to Senator Langer concerning Haji Moosa Ismail
subfiles.about: Explains that Ismail should seek Japanese-entry permission through the Indian foreign authorities.
subfiles.summary: Because India has representation in Japan, Ismail's application must proceed through Indian governmental channels.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Bombay concerning Haji Moosa Ismail
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Bombay
subfiles.about: Directs the consul to advise Ismail to submit his application through India's representative in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Circular No. 8 requires Indian authorities, not the State Department, to sponsor Ismail's request.

subfiles.title: Visa Division comments on the Ismail drafts
subfiles.to: Mr. Meyer and E. B. Hutchison
subfiles.about: Questions whether Ismail should apply through American, Indian, British, or other channels.
subfiles.summary: Alexander warns that consuls may lack instructions and notes that MacArthur acts for all Allies, not solely the United States.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Senator Langer about Ismail
subfiles.about: Proposes directing Ismail to apply to the American consul in Bombay.
subfiles.summary: The draft assumes India lacks representation in Japan and assigns the application to the Bombay consulate.

subfiles.title: Draft letter to Haji Moosa Ismail
subfiles.about: Advises Ismail to request a Japanese military-entry permit through the American consul in Bombay.
subfiles.summary: The draft explains proposed procedures for applicants residing where their governments lack Japanese representation.

subfiles.title: Senator Langer's inquiry concerning Haji Moosa Ismail
subfiles.about: Forwards Ismail's file and asks how his Japanese-entry request can be expedited.
subfiles.summary: Langer seeks State Department assistance for the Bombay merchant's proposed business travel.

subfiles.title: Swiss request for a permit for Alice Kaelin
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Switzerland
subfiles.about: Requests prompt issuance of a military permit for Swiss official Alice Kaelin to resume duty in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Kaelin planned to pass through Washington while returning from Swiss leave to her diplomatic post in Japan.

subfiles.title: Syrian note submitting applications for Faez Abdallah Ejel
subfiles.about: Submits Ejel's applications and mentions earlier requests by Adnan Samman and Rida Rabbat.
subfiles.summary: The Syrian Legation forwards Ejel's forms and notes two other pending Syrian applications.

subfiles.title: Envelope from the Syrian Legation
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Envelope addressed to the Department of State's Special Projects Division.
subfiles.summary: Mailing envelope accompanying Syrian Legation materials.

subfiles.title: Application of Faez Abdallah Ejel to enter Japan
subfiles.from: Faez Abdallah Ejel, through the Syrian Legation
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Requests entry for Ejel to purchase Japanese textiles for firms serving India, Syria, and British West Africa.
subfiles.summary: Ejel describes his passport, textile businesses, intended production-center visits, and export markets.

subfiles.title: Security-check memorandum on Faez Abdallah Ejel
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records negative file checks and an unresolved report that Ejel had been refused a visa at Bermuda.
subfiles.summary: No adverse record was found, although an earlier, misdirected inquiry left the Bermuda visa issue unresolved.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation on Alice Kaelin's clearance
subfiles.about: Records notification to Ochsner that Alice Kaelin was cleared for entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: O'Brien also explained the documentation required under paragraphs 9a and 7b of SCAP Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Ejel's application
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Ejel's application and explains that it will be considered under business-travel quotas.
subfiles.summary: The Syrian Legation will be informed after military review under the Inter-Allied Trade Board quota system.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Ejel's application to military authorities
subfiles.about: Forwards Ejel's application for consideration under the quota for “other” nations.
subfiles.summary: Chappell asks the Military Permit Section to present Ejel's Syrian business application to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Swiss notification of Alice Kaelin's clearance
subfiles.to: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Switzerland
subfiles.about: Confirms no military objection to Kaelin's travel and explains the required entry statement.
subfiles.summary: The note cites SCAP Circular No. 8 and directs the Swiss Legation to document Kaelin's clearance and travel particulars.

subfiles.title: Military-permit application for Alice Kaelin
subfiles.from: E. B. Hutchison, Exit Permit Unit
subfiles.about: Requests a permit for Kaelin to resume employment with the Swiss diplomatic mission in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The form records Kaelin's Swiss passport, destination, employment, and intended September departure.

subfiles.title: Military clearance for Alice Kaelin
subfiles.about: States that there is no military objection to Alice Kaelin's travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Civil Affairs Division authorizes notification of Kaelin's clearance.

subfiles.title: Note to Argentina concerning Nakamatsu-family repatriation
subfiles.from: Norman Armour, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests Argentina's guarantee of passage for three Nakamatsu family members seeking repatriation from Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: The note adds Arturo Kazuo Nakamatsu to the prior cases of María and Guillermo and explains their lack of transportation funds.

subfiles.title: Yokohama airgram on Nakamatsu-family repatriation
subfiles.about: Reports that María Nakamatsu seeks Argentine repatriation for herself, her son, and her nephew.
subfiles.summary: The airgram requests Argentina's financial guarantee and instructions because the family cannot pay passage from Okinawa.

subfiles.title: Military clearance for Reverend James Doyle
subfiles.about: Reports no military objection to Reverend James Doyle's travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Doyle is cleared despite the Military Permit Section having received no formal application.

subfiles.title: Syrian note submitting Adnan Samman's applications
subfiles.about: Submits two application forms for Syrian citizen Adnan Samman to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The note recalls that Samman's entry request was first presented to the Legation on June 7.

subfiles.title: Application of Adnan Samman to enter Japan
subfiles.from: M. A. Adnan Samman, through the Syrian ambassador
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Requests six months in Tokyo to buy Japanese textiles and yarns for Middle Eastern firms.
subfiles.summary: Samman supplies his Syrian passport, planned route, business purpose, and the Damascus firms he represents.

subfiles.title: Security-check memorandum on Adnan Samman
subfiles.from: M. E. Wolberg, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records that departmental searches found no information on Samman or the three firms he represented.
subfiles.summary: Security and economic files contained no record of Samman or his named Damascus firms.

subfiles.title: Muller & Phipps letter concerning William Rawnsley
subfiles.about: Submits Rawnsley's passport after Commerce approval and requests prompt validation for Japanese travel.
subfiles.summary: Muller & Phipps expects Rawnsley to join the second business contingent in mid-September.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation on Rawnsley's pending clearance
subfiles.about: Records Keough's explanation that Rawnsley awaited SCAP approval because the United States business quota was full.
subfiles.summary: Rawnsley was among eighty Commerce-approved names sent to SCAP, but quota congestion delayed authorization.

subfiles.title: Reply to Broderick concerning Rawnsley
subfiles.about: Explains that Rawnsley's SCAP approval remains pending because the American business quota is overloaded.
subfiles.summary: The Department will retain Rawnsley's passport and endorse it when clearance arrives.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Samman's application
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Samman's application and explains its review under Inter-Allied Trade Board quotas.
subfiles.summary: The Syrian Legation will be notified after military authorities decide Samman's application.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Samman's application to military authorities
subfiles.about: Forwards Samman's application for consideration under the quota for “other” nations.
subfiles.summary: Chappell asks the Military Permit Section to present Samman's Syrian business application to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing William Zamara's Japanese visit
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Authorizes Zamara's entry during November 16–30 for a twenty-one-day stay and prescribes substitute documentation.
subfiles.summary: The embassy may certify the telegram because no Czech representative is available in Bangkok.

subfiles.title: Nour Trading Company letter submitting Nourafchan's forms
subfiles.about: Submits five alien-departure applications completed by Elias Nourafchan at the United States consulate in Milan.
subfiles.summary: The company expects Nourafchan to return to New York and depart for Japan in October.

subfiles.title: Alien departure application of Elias Nourafchan
subfiles.about: Applies to leave the United States for Japanese business travel and subsequent Middle Eastern trade.
subfiles.summary: Nourafchan provides his Iranian passport, residence, finances, references, trade plans, and intention to return after two or three months.

subfiles.title: Office memorandum on Nourafchan's military permit
subfiles.about: Records that Nourafchan's permit allowed entry October 16–30 and asks how it should be delivered.
subfiles.summary: Commerce was contacted to learn whether Nourafchan would collect the permit or receive it by mail.

subfiles.title: Internal note on Nourafchan's reentry concern
subfiles.about: Reports Nourafchan's concern that onward travel to India might prevent his return to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Nourafchan had SCAP clearance for October 16–30 but needed advice on United States reentry after visiting India.

subfiles.title: Routing note transmitting Nourafchan material
subfiles.about: Transmits an attachment for review and confirmation of Spencer's understanding.
subfiles.summary: Brief routing note accompanying Nourafchan-related paperwork.

subfiles.title: Passport Division memorandum forwarding Nourafchan's approvals
subfiles.to: Mr. Williams, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce approval and the military permit for alien traveler Elias Nourafchan.
subfiles.summary: The attached approvals are sent to Protective Services for appropriate action.

subfiles.title: Application for permission to visit Japan by Nourafchan and Frangi
subfiles.from: Elias Nourafchan and Nassim Frangi, Nour Trading Company
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Provides firm, capitalization, merchandise, and prewar Japanese-trade information for Nourafchan and Frangi.
subfiles.summary: The form records Nour Trading Company's textile, carpet, seed, and skin trade and its prior dealings with Japan.
